title: Download your data
summary: Export your reviews, diary listens, and boards as CSV or JSON from your profile settings.
changes: Open Edit Profile and choose CSV or JSON next to Reviews, Listens, or Boards. The file downloads straight away.
CSV files open cleanly in Excel, Numbers, and Google Sheets. JSON keeps everything exactly as written.
Board exports list albums in the same order as the board, and empty boards are included.
Album titles and artists match the catalog as it is today. Listens of albums that have since been removed are left out, and the JSON file says how many.
You can download up to 10 exports an hour.

title: Approve suggestions in bulk
summary: Moderators can approve several community suggestions at once from the suggestion queue.
changes: Tick the box beside a pending suggestion, or use Select all, then choose Approve selected. Up to 20 can be approved at a time.
Each suggestion is approved as proposed: new albums are added, corrections apply every proposed change, and genre suggestions apply every change.
Suggestions that need a closer look, such as possible duplicates or genre names that don't exist yet, have no checkbox and still need to be opened and approved on their own.
Each suggestion succeeds or fails on its own. Anything that wasn't approved shows the reason under its card, and contributors are notified for each approval as usual.

title: Edit your reviews
summary: Change a review's rating or text after you post it.
changes: Edit your own review from the album page, the review's own page, or your reviews shelf.
Edited reviews show an "edited" tag. Hover over it to see when.
An edit keeps the review's original date and place in feeds, and doesn't notify anyone again.
Album ratings update as soon as you save.

title: Faster pages
summary: Rescened loads faster, especially the home page, album pages, and profiles.
changes: The first visit downloads about 40% less code, and each page loads the rest when you open it.
Album covers load as you scroll instead of all at once.
Search checks MusicBrainz at the same time as Rescened, so discovery results appear sooner.
Home page lists, profiles, and board lists load faster.
A profile still shows everything else if one section fails to load.
Review feeds and follower lists show everyone's names, not just the first 10 people.

title: Talk about reviews
summary: Comment on any review and reply to other people's comments, right on the review page.
changes: Open a review to read its comments and add your own. Replies sit under the comment they answer, and replying to a reply names the person you're answering.
Review cards show how many comments a review has. Click the count to jump to the conversation.
Edit or delete your own comments. A deleted comment that has replies leaves a placeholder so the conversation still makes sense.
Get notified when someone comments on your review or replies to you. Both can be turned off in notification settings.
Report a comment that breaks the rules, and a moderator will review it.
Comments are public, including on private profiles, and show your name.

title: Put your boards in your own order
summary: Arrange the albums on a board however you like, or turn it into a numbered ranking.
changes: Switch a board's Order from Date added to Custom order, then drag albums or use the arrow buttons to move them, and save.
Turn on Show as a ranked list to number a board's albums. Visitors see the numbers too, and the board card says Ranked list.
Board covers and previews follow your order, so a top ten shows your top four.
New albums go to the bottom of a board in custom order.
Custom order works on boards of up to 100 albums. If a board grows past 100, it keeps its order for the first 100, and later albums follow by date added.

title: More useful notifications
summary: Find out when a suggestion is reviewed or when someone you follow reviews an album on your boards, and choose what you get notified about.
changes: When a moderator approves your suggestion, asks for changes, rejects it, or marks it as a duplicate, you get a notification that links straight to it.
When someone you follow reviews an album that's on one of your boards, you'll hear about it.
Notification settings let you turn off likes, follows, or reviews from people you follow. Suggestion updates always stay on, so you never miss a request for changes.
Mark everything read or clear your notifications from the Notifications page, and load older ones with Load more.
Likes on your reviews now open the review itself.

title: A queue for what you play next
summary: Line up to 15 albums you want to hear next, in the order you want to hear them.
changes: Use Add to queue on any album page to put it at the end of your queue, or Listen next to put it first.
Reorder your queue by dragging or with the arrow buttons on your home page or profile, then save the new order.
Logging a listen takes that album off your queue automatically, including listens logged from Last.fm.
Pick something for me on your boards can now add its pick to your queue. An album already in your queue keeps its place.
Your profile shows what’s up next, and visitors can see your whole queue. Private profiles keep it to you.
The single Listening Next album from Edit Profile becomes the first album in your queue.

title: Genres, shaped by the community
summary: Albums now have genres, and anyone can suggest them. Browse a genre, search inside one, and see your own top genres.
changes: Genres appear under each album’s title, with the main genre highlighted. Tap one to open its genre page.
Use Suggest genres on any album to add or remove genres and pick the main one. Search finds genres by any of their names, so “rap” finds Hip hop.
Can’t find the right genre? Propose up to two new ones per suggestion. A moderator reviews every change before anyone sees it.
If a moderator asks for changes, the album page links straight to your suggestion so you can revise it.
Genre pages list albums by highest rated or most recently reviewed, include sub-genres like Jazz rap under Hip hop, and link to related genres.
Search within a genre from its page to find albums that match both.
Your Stats tab now shows your top genres.
Moderators review genre suggestions in the suggestion queue, can map a new name onto an existing genre, and maintain the genre list from a new Genres page.

title: Your listening stats
summary: A new Stats tab on every profile sums up the last two years of listening, reviewing, and saving.
changes: See total listens, albums, days listened, your longest streak, and an estimate of hours listened.
A month-by-month chart shows when you listened most, along with your busiest day of the week.
Find your top albums and artists, and which decades your music comes from.
Review stats show your rating spread, how many of the albums you heard you reviewed, how your ratings compare with everyone else's, and your most-liked review.
Pick the last two years or a single year, and turn automatically logged listens on or off.
Stats are visible on public profiles. Private profiles keep them to the owner.

title: Your take on track rankings
summary: See how your track ranking compares with everyone else’s, rank with the people you follow, and find each album’s fan favorite.
changes: After you rank an album, the community view shows how much you agree with other listeners and your hottest take: the track you rate most differently.
Arrows next to each track show whether you rank it higher or lower than everyone else.
Switch the community view to People you follow to see standings from just your circle. Private profiles aren’t counted there.
Standings based on fewer than three rankings are marked Early, since the order can still change a lot.
Once enough people agree, the top track gets a Fan favorite badge on the album page.
A new Rankings tab on profiles lists every album someone has ranked, with their top three tracks.
Ranking an album now shows up in profile activity and in your network feed.

title: A diary calendar, shareable reviews, and smarter boards
summary: See your listening month at a glance, share any review with its own link, and let Rescened pick something from your backlog.
changes: Open the new Diary tab on any profile to see a month of listens as a calendar. Tap a day to see what was played.
Every review has its own page now. Use Share on a review, an album, a profile, or a board to copy its link.
Sort reviews by highest or lowest rating, as well as latest and most liked.
Not sure what to play? “Pick something for me” suggests a saved album you haven’t logged or reviewed yet, from all your boards or just one.
Add a short description to any board, and sort a board’s albums by date added, release year, artist, title, or listens.
Album pages show your own rating, the average from people you follow, the track count and total runtime, and the label.
Tap a follower in “Reviewed by people you follow” to jump straight to their review.

title: Rank an album’s tracks
summary: Put an album’s songs in your own order and see which tracks the community rates highest, plus a round of fixes from your feedback.
changes: Open the new Ranking tab on any album with a tracklist to rank every track or just your favorites.
Drag tracks into place, or use the arrows on a phone, then save. You can change or remove your ranking anytime.
The community view scores each track by where listeners tend to place it.
Search the Recently approved page by album title or artist.
Album suggestions and corrections save your draft as you type, so nothing is lost if you leave the page.
Profile review counts and average ratings now reflect all of your reviews, not just the ones on screen.
Expired Last.fm sessions are hidden by default, with an option to show them.
The Last.fm tab on your profile uses white backgrounds in light mode.

title: Last.fm listen detection and your listening diary
summary: Connect Last.fm and Rescened can spot when you’ve listened to a full album, then help you keep a diary of what you’ve heard.
changes: Connect Last.fm from the new tab on your profile. It’s rolling out to a small group first.
An album counts as listened once you play at least 80% of its standard tracks.
Log a detected listen to your diary or dismiss it, or turn on automatic logging.
Automatically logged entries are labeled, and you can change their date or delete them.

title: A home for what’s new
summary: Follow along as Rescened grows. Patch notes bring new features, improvements, and fixes together in one place.
changes: Open Patch notes from the navigation bar, whether you’re signed in or just browsing.
Read the latest updates first, with earlier releases kept here to explore.
